items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: And we had, uh, Charlie Love, John Robeshoe, himself on the band, on the violin, and Harrison Bones on trombone.

ctx.x: Who was in that at that time?

Let's see, John Robeshoe Band, we had, let's see, now we had Old Man McCurtis, he's dead, Willie Humphrey, George Augustine on bass, Mercedes Goldman on piano, and we had, let's see, John, you see, was playing banjo with John Robeshoe. And then we had, sometimes Willie Paglia was to play trumpet. Uh-huh. And we had, uh, Charlie Love, John Robeshoe, himself on the band, on the violin, and Harrison Bones on trombone. Oh, yeah. items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: And I think he had Charlie loved playing trumpet, if I'm not mistaken.

ctx.x: Someone say he's living, some say he's dead. In fact, I don't know, I don't know where he's in contact. Yeah, I haven't been. Wouldn't know where to contact Bob. I haven't seen Bob in about five years. But we worked all down in Buris, and then we called a place to call it down, this place down in Seminole Parish, they call it, not Buris, Delico Island.
